whyItMatters: A lifecycle config becomes operationally significant once it is attached to a notebook. At that point, the startup script has a live execution path into a SageMaker environment.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may attach a malicious or modified lifecycle config to a notebook to prepare code execution when the notebook next starts.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is attractive because it converts a configuration artifact into a live startup mechanism without immediately running code.
threatContext.whyItMatters: Association is a stronger signal than lifecycle-config mutation alone because it shows the config is being put into position for execution.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may not realize that a risky lifecycle config has become active on a notebook environment.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for SageMaker
loggingRequirements: CreateNotebookInstance and UpdateNotebookInstance events must be ingested.
The detector should evaluate whether lifecycleConfigName is present and non-empty.
Notebook start events should be available for later execution-path correlation.
limitations: Association alone does not guarantee the notebook has started yet.
Some approved notebook provisioning workflows will legitimately attach lifecycle configs.
The notebook and config risk still require enrichment for prioritization.

enrichment.description: Classify the notebook by environment, owner, and data sensitivity.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Raises urgency when risky configs are attached to important notebooks.

enrichment.description: Determine whether the attached config is approved, expected, or newly introduced.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Separates known-good startup logic from suspicious attachment.

enrichment.description: Track whether the notebook is started or restarted soon after the association.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Improves confidence that the attached code is about to run.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should detect the operational attachment of a lifecycle config to a SageMaker notebook. It should match notebook create or update events only when `lifecycleConfigName` is set, because that is the point where startup logic becomes executable on the notebook.
conditions: requestParameters.lifecycleConfigName exists and is not empty
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Require an actual lifecycle-config attachment. 2. Resolve notebook criticality and config approval state. 3. Correlate with notebook start or post-start sensitive activity for higher-confidence detections.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when a lifecycle config is associated with a notebook instance, especially on sensitive notebooks or when the config is newly changed or unapproved.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium depending on notebook provisioning patterns

deployment.scheduling: Real-time is useful because notebook start often follows shortly after association.
considerations: This is the operational handoff rule for SageMaker lifecycle configs.
Notebook inventory and config approval state are key enrichments.
